sections.content: The gerund is the natural tool for showing two things happening at once — a missionary teaching while learning a language, a community producing goods while developing a musical tradition. It can open the sentence or sit right after the subject. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Enseñando la doctrina cristiana mientras aprendían y usaban el idioma guaraní, los jesuitas lograron una relación menos violenta.
items.english: Teaching Christian doctrine while learning and using the Guaraní language, the Jesuits achieved a less violent relationship.

items.spanish: Estas comunidades, produciendo tejidos y ganado mientras desarrollaban una notable tradición musical, llegaron a ser económicamente prósperas.
items.english: These communities, producing textiles and cattle while developing a notable musical tradition, became economically prosperous.

items.spanish: Las reducciones, dependiendo casi por completo de la administración jesuita, entraron en rápida decadencia tras la expulsión.
items.english: The missions, depending almost entirely on Jesuit administration, fell into rapid decline after the expulsion.

items.spanish: Vigilando la ortodoxia religiosa mientras construía hospitales, escuelas y universidades, la Iglesia funcionó como una de las instituciones más poderosas del imperio.
items.english: Monitoring religious orthodoxy while building hospitals, schools and universities, the Church functioned as one of the empire's most powerful institutions.

sections.content: When two gerunds appear joined by mientras (enseñando... mientras aprendían), notice the tense shift is fine — mientras can connect a gerund to a full conjugated verb, not just another gerund. The two actions just need to overlap in time, not match grammatically.
